questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Growing up in Mumbai, Nehal’s childhood was _______ with memories of playing in gardens and nurturing plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**filled**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**filled**" is the correct choice as it accurately conveys the idea of Nehal's childhood being imbued with memories.
 
• The option "**full**" is incorrect because it is generally used as an adjective, not as a past participle for this context.
 
• The option "**filling**" is incorrect as it does not fit grammatically in the sentence.
 
• The option "**fills**" is incorrect because it is present tense, whereas the sentence requires a past participle.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Growing up in Mumbai, Nehal’s childhood was filled__ with memories of playing in gardens and nurturing plants.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Full (पूर्ण)**: Used as an adjective to describe something that is complete or has reached its capacity.
 
• **Filling (भरना)**: A present participle, used to describe an ongoing action, and is not suitable for this sentence.
 
• **Fills (भरता है)**: A present tense verb, which does not fit the past context of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Your tongue gives you information about the taste of food, but your sense of smell also plays an important role when you breathe air out ______ eating.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank in the sentence is appropriately filled with the word "**while**," which indicates the action happening simultaneously during eating.
 
• Option 1 "**with**" does not fit the context as it refers to accompaniment.
 
• Option 2 "**in**" does not make sense in the sentence construction.
 
• Option 4 "**from**" would be incorrect as it implies direction or origin.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Your tongue gives you information about the taste of food, but your sense of smell also plays an important role when you breathe air out while__ eating.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **With:** Indicates accompaniment or association but is not appropriate here.
 
• **In:** Suggests location or involvement but does not fit the sentence.
 
• **From:** Refers to direction or origin, which is unrelated to the context.
 
• **While:** Indicates simultaneous action, making it the most suitable option.

Placate
questions.solution:

questions.question:
The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with an adverbial usage error.

Christopher told Mathew, / "Politely, she / takes the bus / to work."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. "Politely, she".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"politely"** is used as an adverb and is incorrectly placed at the beginning of the sentence, modifying the subject **"she"** instead of the action **"takes the bus."**
 
• Adverbs that describe the manner of an action are typically placed closer to the verb they modify, ensuring the meaning is clear.
 
• The correct placement of the adverb would be: **"She takes the bus politely to work."**

Correct sentence: *Christopher told Mathew, "She takes the bus politely to work."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adverb Placement Rules:**
 
 
• **Before the verb:** Adverbs like "always," "never," and "often" are placed before the main verb. Example: She **always** takes the bus.
 
• **After the verb:** Adverbs of manner (like "politely") are typically placed after the verb they modify. Example: She takes the bus **politely**.
 
• **At the beginning:** Some adverbs (like "fortunately" or "sadly") can be placed at the beginning of a sentence to modify the whole sentence. Example: **Fortunately**, she reached on time.

A) The supervisor advised / B) him to focus on the / C) examination first and / D) submit the assignment latter.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The error lies in segment **D) submit the assignment latter.**
 
• The word **"latter"** is incorrect in this context. The correct word should be **"later"**, as "later" refers to a time in the future, whereas "latter" refers to the second of two items mentioned.
 
• Thus, the correct sentence is: *"The supervisor advised him to focus on the examination first and submit the assignment **later**."*

Correct sentence: *The supervisor advised him to focus on the examination first and submit the assignment **later**.*

• **Later:** Refers to a point in time in the future. Example: "I will call you later."
 
• **Latter:** Refers to the second of two things previously mentioned. Example: "Between tea and coffee, I prefer the latter."
 
 
 
• Always ensure that the word used in a sentence aligns with its intended meaning to avoid such errors.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence and rectify it. If no correction is needed, select ‘No correction required’.

The article__ publishes__ in the newspaper today.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. has been published .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence, "The article publishes in the newspaper today," is in the present tense, but it describes an action that has already occurred and is relevant to the present.
 
• To convey this accurately, the present perfect tense is required. The present perfect tense is formed using **"has been" + past participle**.
 
• The correct phrase is **"has been published"**, which indicates that the article was published recently and is relevant at the time of speaking.

Correct sentence: *The article has been published in the newspaper today*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Perfect Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Has/Have + Past Participle.
 
• **Example:** She has completed her homework.
 
• **Usage: **Used for actions that occurred in the past but are relevant to the present moment.
 
 
 
• **Past Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + Verb (Past Form).
 
• **Example:** He went to the market yesterday.
 
• **Usage:** Describes completed actions that occurred in the past.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**disappearance**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence indicates that the "Second Anglo-Maratha War had shattered the power of the Maratha chiefs but not their spirit." This implies a loss or vanishing of their previous state of freedom and independence.
 
• The phrase "rankled in their hearts" suggests a deep resentment or irritation caused by this state.
 
• They then made a "last desperate attempt to regain their independence and old prestige," further supporting the idea that something related to their freedom was no longer present.
 
• "**Disappearance**" (Option 3) is the most fitting noun. It directly conveys that their freedom or the state of being free had ceased to exist or become invisible, which would indeed cause deep emotional distress and a desire to regain it.
 
• "Lost" (Option 1) is a verb or adjective; it is grammatically incorrect to be a noun in the structure "The _____ of their freedom." The noun form would be "loss."
 
• "Benefit" (Option 2) means an advantage, which contradicts the negative feeling implied by "rankled."
